questions.stem: What is Process Modelling, often called Business Process Modelling (BPM)?
options: The practice of describing how work is carried out step by step inside an organisation
The practice of designing database tables
The practice of choosing a workflow vendor
The practice of measuring server performance
The practice of writing business strategy
questions.explanation: Process Modelling describes how work is carried out step by step, visually representing workflows, activities and decision points.

questions.stem: How does Process Modelling differ from Business Modelling?
options: Process Modelling focuses on data structures; Business Modelling on workflows
Process Modelling is technology-specific; Business Modelling is not
They are the same technique under two names
Business Modelling is more detailed than Process Modelling
Business Modelling explains the business at a high level; Process Modelling focuses on the actual flow of work
questions.explanation: Business Modelling explains what the business does at a high level, while Process Modelling explains how the work actually happens.

questions.stem: What is the main goal of Process Modelling?
options: To reduce data redundancy
To define a shared vocabulary
To design star schemas
To assign database permissions
To analyse and improve business processes
questions.explanation: The main goal is to analyse and improve business processes by documenting each step so delays, repeated tasks and unclear responsibilities become visible.

questions.stem: In the school library example of Process Modelling, what happens if the requested book is not available?
options: The book is issued anyway
The librarian orders a new copy
The student is informed to try again later
The student is added to a database
The process restarts from the beginning
questions.explanation: If the book is not available, the student is informed to try again later; the decision is made based on availability.

questions.stem: In the loan approval example of Process Modelling, which step follows the credit department's credit check?
options: The customer submits the application
The loan officer collects documents
The finance department disburses the funds
A risk manager reviews and decides whether to approve or reject
The collections team monitors repayments
questions.explanation: After the credit check, a risk manager reviews the information and decides whether to approve or reject the loan.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a decision rule in Process Modelling?
options: Storing the customer's address in a table
Escalating an application to a senior risk officer if the loan amount exceeds a defined threshold
Naming the workflow tool
Backing up the loan database nightly
Publishing a dashboard of branch performance
questions.explanation: Decision rules guide the flow, for example rejecting a loan when the credit score is below a value or escalating when the amount is above a threshold.

questions.stem: Which measurement is given as an analytical use of Process Modelling?
options: The average time taken from loan application to approval
The number of columns in the loan table
The size of the database in gigabytes
The salary of the loan officer
The number of servers in use
questions.explanation: Analysts may measure the average time from application to approval, the number of escalations or common rejection reasons to find bottlenecks.

questions.stem: Process Modelling often acts as a bridge between which two things?
options: Storage and compute
Business requirements and system design
Raw data and metadata
Sales and marketing
On-premises and cloud
questions.explanation: Because it shows who performs each task and how work is handed over, Process Modelling bridges business requirements and system design.

questions.stem: Which statement about the nature of Process Modelling is correct?
options: It focuses on data structures rather than workflows
It can only be created at a highly detailed level
It is generally independent of technology, although often implemented using workflow or automation tools
It requires a specific database engine
It cannot be used for compliance checks
questions.explanation: Process Modelling focuses on workflows rather than data structures and is generally technology-independent, though often implemented with workflow or automation tools.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT something Process Modelling is said to make work?
options: Visible
Measurable
Improvable
Normalised
All of these are named
questions.explanation: Process Modelling makes work visible, measurable and improvable; normalisation is a data modelling concept.
